## Answer: no, it ships nothing

`crimes scan --format json` flags it explicitly — **`crime_00011` / `missing_agent_context` ("Missing Agent Context")**, medium severity, confidence 0.90, `agent_risk` 0.47, pack `universal`:

```
no AGENTS.md found at repo root
no CLAUDE.md found at repo root
no .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md present
no .agents/skills/*/SKILL.md present
package.json declares bin(s): tsup, tsup-node — agents have no way to discover commands
```

One note on reading the JSON: the finding's `file` is `assets/cjs_shims.js`, which is just an anchor — this is a repo-level finding, not a problem with that file. And despite the name `04-monorepo`, `coverage.by_package` only surfaces `assets` and `test` with all source under `src/`, so a single root `AGENTS.md` is sufficient here; you don't need per-package files.

## Why this matters for your first PR

The rest of the scan is the argument for why this particular repo is a bad one to enter blind. Three things an agent has no way to learn from the code alone:

**1. The test suite gives false confidence.** 26 of 87 findings are `weak_test_signal` — 12 tests with **zero** `expect`/`assert` calls (`test/example.test.ts`, `test/graphql.test.ts`, `test/shims.test.ts`, `test/tsconfig.test.ts`, `test/experimental-dts.test.ts`) and 14 more using only weak matchers. A green run does not mean your change is safe, and nothing in the repo says so.

**2. Safe-sounding functions delete files.** Four `name_behavior_mismatch` findings — `getRollupConfig` (`src/rollup.ts:38`), `build` (`src/index.ts:167`), `buildAll` (`src/index.ts:291`), `buildStart` (`src/rollup.ts:77`) — all call `removeFiles`. An agent reading `getRollupConfig` as a pure accessor and hoisting or duplicating the call would silently delete output directories.

**3. The load-bearing files aren't marked.** `src/utils.ts` (fan-in 18), `src/plugin.ts` (fan-in 10), `src/log.ts` (fan-in 9), `src/index.ts` (fan-out 17), `src/esbuild/index.ts` (fan-out 11). Compounding this, the biggest functions exceed any sane context window for a targeted edit — `build` at 293 lines, `runEsbuild` at 237, `mainTasks` at 194. An agent that loads 60 lines of a 293-line function and edits confidently is the exact failure mode here.

Without an AGENTS.md, every agent rediscovers (or fails to rediscover) all of this on each session, and the discovery is invisible in the PR diff.

## Minimal AGENTS.md skeleton

Root-level `AGENTS.md`. This is the smallest version that clears `missing_agent_context` and actually earns its place — the detector only checks existence, but a stub that lies is worse than nothing. Placeholders marked `TODO` need filling from `package.json` `scripts`; I've left them rather than guess, since the scan JSON only tells me the declared bins are `tsup` / `tsup-node`.

```markdown
# AGENTS.md

Build tool that compiles TS/JS bundles. Published binaries: `tsup`, `tsup-node`.

## Commands

- Install: `TODO` (pnpm / npm / yarn — check packageManager field)
- Build: `TODO`
- Test: `TODO`
- Typecheck: `TODO`
- Lint: `TODO`

Run build + test before proposing any change.

## Layout

- `src/index.ts` — entry point; `build()` orchestrates the whole pipeline
- `src/esbuild/` — esbuild path and its plugins (postcss, svelte, swc)
- `src/rollup.ts`, `src/rollup/` — rollup path, used for .d.ts generation
- `src/plugin.ts` — plugin lifecycle hooks
- `src/utils.ts`, `src/log.ts` — shared helpers, imported nearly everywhere
- `test/` — integration tests; `test/utils.ts` holds shared fixtures

## Before you edit

Treat these as load-bearing. Prefer additive changes; read the importers first.

- `src/utils.ts` — 18 importers
- `src/plugin.ts` — 10 importers
- `src/log.ts` — 9 importers
- `src/index.ts` — imports 17 modules; `build()` is ~290 lines, read it whole
- `test/utils.ts` — 9 test files depend on it

## Safety rules

- `removeFiles()` deletes from disk. It is called by `build`, `buildAll`,
  `buildStart`, and `getRollupConfig` — despite those names. Never hoist,
  reorder, or duplicate a call to it.
- Tests are integration-level and build real output. Several assert nothing
  at all. A passing suite is weak evidence — verify behaviour manually for
  anything touching output paths or the dts pipeline.
- `experimentalDts` is under active change; its tests are the weakest in
  the repo.

## Conventions

- `TODO` — commit message format, changeset requirement, branch naming
```

I have not written this to the fixture — `evals/fixtures/04-monorepo` is an eval input, and adding the file would change what future runs of this scenario measure.

## Verifying it cleared

```bash
crimes scan --format json | jq '.findings[] | select(.type == "missing_agent_context")'
```

Empty output means the finding is gone. Expected summary shift: `total` 87 → 86, `medium` 38 → 37.
